title: TJX just posted its biggest day since 2020 after beating on sales andcomps. Is off-price retail actually winning, or is this a one-day pop?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
\[TJX\]([https://tickeron.com/ticker/TJX/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/TJX/)) jumped 10.04% in the midday  
write-up, from Tuesday's close of $129.85 to $142.89, on pace for its  
largest single-day gain since November 2020. Later prints were a bit  
softer, around +9% near $141.75.  
  
The catalyst was fiscal Q3 results before the open: net sales of  
$15.95 billion beat the roughly $15.84 billion consensus, consolidated  
comparable sales rose 4% versus about 2.9–3.0% expected, and Marmaxx  
comps accelerated to 2% from 1% in Q2. The whole off-price group  
caught a bid, including \[BURL\]([https://tickeron.com/ticker/BURL/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/BURL/)).  
  
Why \[TJX\]([https://tickeron.com/ticker/TJX/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/TJX/)) had its biggest day in  
years, including the comps and the Marmaxx detail:  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-the-tjx-companies-tjx-stock-up-10-04-today-40385/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-the-tjx-companies-tjx-stock-up-10-04-today-40385/)  
  
Does a beat like this change the retail story, or is a 10% bounce just  
relief after a rough tape?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from today's midday write-up, not a  
live quote.
